title: AI agents in the lab: aptamers and proteins designed in a closed loop
summary: AI agents designed DNA aptamers and protein binders, which were then tested in the lab over multiple rounds. Target success rates reached 33.5% for myoglobin and 42.1% for α-thrombin (98.5% specificity). The post summarizes three arXiv papers whose peer review is unconfirmed; it also reports initial failures.

evidence.tested: Agents ran three design-test-iterate rounds of DNA aptamers against myoglobin and alpha-thrombin in the lab, reaching 33.5% and 42.1% hit rates with 98.5% specificity for thrombin; protein binders against FAP were reported at single-digit nanomolar affinity.
evidence.unknown: Peer review of the cited arXiv papers is unconfirmed; there are two protein targets and three rounds; initial rounds failed, and protein expression adds steps to each loop.
evidence.ai_role: Agents designed and revised sequences across rounds and adjusted design rules after reading wet-lab data, under human oversight of protocols and robot runs.
